chunks: Signals inductors pass and block. The question: What sort of signals can inductors pass through and block? What sort of filter behavior is this?
An inductor lets slow signals through and holds back fast ones. At DC, which never changes, it acts like a plain wire. As the signal changes faster, the inductor fights it more.
That is why inductors are used to smooth out power and to filter out noise. It is the opposite of a capacitor, which blocks DC and passes fast signals.
Picture a heavy door. If you push it slowly and steadily, it moves along with you and hardly resists.
If you try to shake it back and forth quickly, its weight fights every change of direction, and it barely moves. A slowly changing current is like the slow push, so it passes.
A quickly changing signal is like the shaking, and the inductor blocks it.
Left: L in series with the signal; at high frequency its impedance is large, so little reaches R L.
Right: L shunting to ground; at low frequency it shorts the signal away, at high frequency it's open and the signal passes. This is the dual of the capacitor circuits.
